messages.subject: Multispectral: Removing the soil and weeds in eucalyptus forests no nice results
parts:
First, thanks for this nice and agro-revolutionary package!!!

I make some tests using multispectral Parrot Sequoia  - Green (550 BP 40), Red (660 BP 40), Red Edge (735 BP 10) and Near infrared (790 BP 40) in eucalyptus plantations. But I'd like to know how I can perform my output because there are a lot of trees loosing  in the default fieldMask() function?

In my example:

EX.Klabin<-stack("parrot_kablin_orto.tif")
EX.Klabin.RemSoil<- fieldMask(mosaic = EX.Klabin, Red = 1, Green = 2, Blue = 3, index = "HUE")
EX3.RemSoil<-fieldMask(EX.Klabin.RemSoil$newMosaic,mask = EX.Klabin.RemSoil$mask ,cropValue=0,cropAbove=T,plot=T) # Removing weeds from senescence stage with flowering mask
#
Output:

messages.subject: Re: Multispectral: Removing the soil and weeds in eucalyptus forests no nice results
parts:
Thank you foresteyebrazil for asking and thank you Kassim for answering.

It is exactly what Kassim explained ... You should change the "index" and the "cropValue" to find each is the best combination for your data. Histograms visualizations normally help a lot to identify which value you should to use at "cropValue" parameter. There is a better explanation with examples about this process at this link: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6. 

Please read this part:

"Sugestion: This function could also be used to build an index to remove soil or weeds. First it is necessary to identify the threshold to differentiate soil from the plant material. At the example below (B), all values above 0.7 were considered as soil and further removed using fieldMask (C & D)."

EX1.Indices.BGI<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX1.Rotated, index = c("BGI")) 
dev.off() 
hist(EX1.Indices.BGI$BGI) # Image segmentation start from 0.7 (soil and plants) 
EX1.BGI<- fieldMask(mosaic = EX1.Rotated, Red = 1, Green = 2, Blue = 3, index = "BGI", cropValue = 0.7, cropAbove = T) 

Let us know if you have any other question,
Filipe

messages.subject: Image segmentation applied to find a calculated cropValue
parts:
Hi Everyone,

In the fieldimageR example:

EX1<-stack("EX1_RGB.tif")
plotRGB(EX1, r = 1, g = 2, b = 3)
EX1.Crop <- fieldCrop(mosaic = EX1) # For heavy images (large, high resolution, etc.) p
EX1.Rotated<-fieldRotate(mosaic = EX1.Crop, clockwise = F)
hist(EX1.Indices.BGI$BGI) # Image segmentation start from 0.7 (soil and plants)

Here I have in example 0.7 as the threshold, but there is some function or mathematical resource for the exact value calculation using EX1.Indices.BGI$BGI data set?

Thanks,

Alexandre

messages.subject: Re: Image segmentation applied to find a calculated cropValue
parts:
Hi Alexandre,

There are different methods to do image segmentation in R, for example using cluster analysis. R has one function called kmeans that makes K clusters of pixels according to their value. You can use that to make a mask. However, I like graphic visualizations. I always plot the single layer (plot of the index) and the index histogram to choose my cropValue. 

Let's see what the other members in our community are going to say. Hope someone help us with different ideas...!!!

Thank you for asking,
Filipe

        at this link: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6. 

      


      

      
Please read this part:

      


      

      
"Sugestion: This function could also be used to
        build an index to remove soil or weeds. First it is necessary to
        identify the threshold to differentiate soil from the plant
        material. At the example below (B), all values above 0.7 were
        considered as soil and further removed using fieldMask (C
        & D)."

      


      

      
EX1.Indices.BGI<- fieldIndex(mosaic
          = EX1.Rotated, index = c("BGI")) 

      
dev.off() 

      
hist(EX1.Indices.BGI$BGI) # Image
          segmentation start from 0.7 (soil and plants) 

      
EX1.BGI<- fieldMask(mosaic =
          EX1.Rotated, Red = 1, Green = 2, Blue = 3, index = "BGI",
          cropValue = 0.7, cropAbove = T) 

      


      

      
Let us know if you have any other question,

      
Filipe

Hi Alexandre,

There are different methods to do image segmentation in R, for example using cluster analysis. R has one function called kmeans that makes K clusters of pixels according to their value. You can use that to make a mask. However, I like graphic visualizations. I always plot the single layer (plot of the index) and the index histogram to choose my cropValue. 

Let's see what the other members in our community are going to say. Hope someone help us with different ideas...!!!

Thank you for asking,
Filipe
